newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk sees more high cost power.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk sees more high cost power.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp expects to pay between $28 and $98 per megawatt hour in 1998 for electricity produced by independent power producers.

The utility's 8K filing with the U.S. Securities & Exchange Commission on its agreement to restructure or terminate 44 power purchase contracts included those price projections for the first year of the proposed contract.
Announcing the tentative agreement Monday, the company said it expected to close the transaction by the end of 1997.
It also said "additional information on possible terms for these agreements" was being filed with the SEC.
That filing sets forth "a schedule of possible quantities and prices to be reflected" in contracts now being negotiated with unregulated power producers.
In the filing, Niagara Mohawk said it expects first year purchases of hydro-generated power to total 875 gigawatts at prices ranging from $86 to $98 per megawatt hour.

The utility said it will purchase 353 gigawatts a year of power generated with coal and waste at 28 dollars per megawatt hour and 4,630 gigawatts a year generated with natural gas at $46 per megawatt hour.
It said the price for hydro power is expected to rise to $88 to #100 per megawatt hour in the second year and $114 to $129 in the 20th year of the contracts.
Coal and waste power costs are expected to start rising in the third year and reach $45 per megawatt hour in the 17th year.
Natural gas power costs are also expected to start rising in the third year, but the purchases will end after the 12th year when the cost is expected to be $64 per megawatt hour.
